messages:
olivia: starting a sanity run to compare model-A-v1 (baseline) vs model-A-v2 (quantized) under identical inputs + decoding params. want to rule out runtime decisions (kernel selection, batching policy, KV behavior) as the source of the perf gap.

sam: can you confirm tokenizer snapshot + stop-seq are identical? we've had token count mismatches skewing latencies before.

olivia: yes — same tokenizer hash, same stop sequences. ran token-count diff on our 300 prompt set: 300/300 identical.

javier: did a quick flame/profile on the dedicated pool. kernel_selector picks `int8_conv` for long sequences on v2, but for short sequences it falls back to an fp16 path that does extra transposes. that fallback is surprisingly expensive for the short-tail traffic we care about. sharing sample output below.

javier: ```
$ ./bench --harness replay --workload prompts.json --model model-A-v2 --preserve-timing --clients 8 --batch_limit 64
GPU time per request median: 29.8ms (v1) -> 33.5ms (v2)
Kernel select histogram: fp16_fused: 68%, int8_conv: 22%, fp16_transpose_fallback: 10%
Trace: kv_writes: 4 -> 7 per request (v1 -> v2)
```

liz: interesting — I suspect the batching heuristic is bucketing variable-length requests together, which triggers larger batches and forces paths that thrash KV cache. replay harness preserves arrival spacing so it can expose that.

sam: what harness config did you use? replay vs synthetic poisson?

olivia: replay with preserved timings (exact inter-arrival) and jitter disabled. flags: `--preserve-timing --seed 42 --max-concurrency 64`. also ran a synthetic poisson run to sanity check and saw similar but smaller delta.

perf-bot: Benchmark 2069991234 started by olivia — 3000 reqs, 8 clients, batch_limit=64.

javier: digging into debug logs shows 1.8x KV write ops in v2 due to duplicate cache inserts when batches combine short + long sequences. that increases memory syncs and gpu idle time.

liz: proposed mitigations: 1) pad-aware bucketing to avoid mixing short/long in the same batch, 2) prefer `fp16_fused` kernel for <128 seqs by adjusting kernel selector heuristic, and 3) add a guard in quantized path to avoid the transpose-heavy fallback for common short requests.

sam: can we force a kernel override to confirm hypothesis quickly?

olivia: yes — re-ran with env `REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=fp16_fused` and `REDWOOD_KERNEL_POLICY=static`. pinned decoding params (temp=0.2, top_p=0.95, stop=["\n\n"]) and replay harness same seed.

olivia: run finished. with kernel override v2 median latency now within 3% of baseline and p99 improved ~9%. KV write counts back to baseline.

javier: confirms root cause: interaction between kernel selector + batching heuristic in quantized code path. quantization itself not enough to explain regression.

liz: next steps: add a head-to-head CI check that validates (a) token-count parity, (b) kernel selection distribution for each model variant, and (c) KV write sanity per request. Also implement pad-aware bucketing in batching heuristic.

olivia: filed PERF-4372 with traces, commands, and profiling outputs: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PERF-4372. linked the bench command and full flame traces in the ticket.

sam: nice. small doc ask: update the head-to-head benchmark guide to explicitly call out kernel_selector and batching policy as required fields for reproducible apples-to-apples runs (and include a kernel override recipe).

liz: :thumbsup: I'll take the bucketing change PR. tagging eng-runtime/infra for the CI check.

olivia: thanks all — closing this quick loop. we should add a short test to the replay harness that asserts kernel histogram stability across runs so future patches don't regress silently.
